preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**5 for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]) and all(3 <= int(line.split()[0]) <= 10**6 and 3 <= int(line.split()[1]) <= int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:])
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is an integer t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^5). Each of the next t lines contains two integers n and q (3 ≤ n ≤ 10^6, 3 ≤ q ≤ n) representing the number of cities and the subset size, respectively.

postconditions.expression: all(len(stdout.splitlines()) == t for _ in range(t)) and all(stdout.splitlines()[i] == str(min((n * (n - 1) // 2) - (q * (q - 1) // 2), (n - q + 1) * (q - 1))) for i in range(t) if (n := int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].split()[0])) and (q := int(stdin.splitlines()[i+1].split()[1])))
postconditions.description: For each test case, the output line is the minimum number of roads to demolish, computed as the smaller of (1) the total roads minus the maximum number of edges in a q-clique (q*(q-1)/2), or (2) the maximum number of edges in a graph with n vertices that does not contain a q-clique (Turán-type bound: (n - q + 1) * (q - 1)). This ensures no subset of q cities has all possible roads intact.
